text:
jamie: FYI I flipped the delegated-project-keys canary flag in prod for 10% traffic this morning. want eyes on quota attribution dashboards.
neha: saw it — some requests are still attributing to the org-level key instead of the project key. looks like the routing layer fallback is kicking in.
dave: can you paste an example request id? I can hunt in the router logs.
jamie:  req=01FJ8X9Z5H2 host=api.redwood.example route=auth-proxy -> headers: x-api-key=proj:abc123 x-origin-org=redwood-inc
sophia: quick ask: does the console show project-level billing for that request? the cost dashboard should flip if attribution works.
jamie: console shows org billing for that trace. project ledger empty. :thinking_face:
oliver: probable cause: our auth-exchange returns a temporary service token bound to org when project-scoped SA lookup fails. fallback code path originates from auth-resolver v2.
neha: that explains it — auth-resolver v2 returns claims {org:O123, project:null, sa:unknown} when the SA store times out. router then tags use_org=true.
dave: Timeout was 120ms in the SA lookup. we had transient Redis latency around that time. should we increase lookups to 250ms for canary to reduce noisy fallbacks?
sophia: increasing timeouts hides failures though. UX on console needs to surface fallback events as a telemetry signal so PM/support can see "attributed-via-fallback".
jamie: +1. we should emit an explicit tag on traces: attribution_mode = primary | fallback | proxy. then dashboards can filter.
oliver: can we add that without touching the router? easiest is for auth-proxy to attach claim "_rdw_attrib=fallback" when it sees project==null && org!=null.
neha: good short-term plan. long-term we should make resolver return explicit decision codes: 0=ok,1=timeout,2=not-found. then router interprets.
dave: implementation note: adding a tag is trivial but we also need to change SLO telemetry to count fallback attributions for quota burn and alert on >0.5% fallback rate.
sophia: design question: what should the console show when attribution is fallback? show both org and suggested project? or mark as disputed and surface an action to "inspect raw headers"?
jamie: show both and add a warning badge. users asked for explicit callouts during the beta so they don't get surprised by billing.
oliver: code snippet I ran locally to detect fallback in auth-proxy
```
if claims.get('project') is None and claims.get('org'):
    span.set_tag('rdw.attribution_mode','fallback')
```
dave: for telemetry pipeline, I'll add a fallback boolean to the kafka event schema: "attribution_fallback": true|false. need prod schema migration plan.
neha: pinging @deploy-bot — can we schedule a small deploy that adds the tag to auth-proxy for the canary namespace only?
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy auth-proxy-canary-v1.4.3 to prod-canary at 2024-08-23T14:40:00Z. rolling restart on 3 pods.
sophia: after deploy, I'll update the console line item to show "attribution reason" and wire a filter on the per-route dashboard.
jamie: follow-up: we should run a sweep for quota double-counting cases. fallback attribution should not increment project quotas but should increment org quotas. create a short playbook.
dave: logging action: add a compact log line `ATtribFallback req=%s src=%s` and sample at 1% to avoid log flood.
neha: agree. I'll open a PR for resolver return codes and a small RFC for telemetry fields.
jamie: thanks all. check the dashboard around 14:45 and flag any spikes. :eyes:
oliver: noted, i'll watch the router spans and alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% for 5m.
jamie: closing loop: if we still see mismatches after flag+deploy+console update, escalate to infra on the Redis timeouts.
neha: copy."
